podcast.title: Judgment Night Collaboration with Dinosaur Jr. (1993)
podcast.body: Del the Funky Homosapien collaborated with rock band Dinosaur Jr. for the 1993 *Judgment Night* soundtrack. This pairing was considered radical at the time due to the limited crossover between rock and hip-hop. The project was a major catalyst for the creation of rap rock and nu metal, and helped bridge the divide between rock and hip-hop fans. "The pairings included Pearl Jam and Cypress Hill, Slayer working with Ice Tea, Faith No More and Buella Tribe, Dinosaur Jr., and Del the Funky Homo sapien, 11 collaborations at all."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Gorillaz Debut Album Collaboration
podcast.body: Del the Funky Homosapien contributed as a rapper to the Gorillaz's debut album and was featured on the single "Clint Eastwood." In Gorillaz lore, he is identified as "Del the ghost rapper," one of the spirits inhabiting Russell Hobbs, and is visually depicted as a blue phantom in the music video. "Damon, being responsible for the music, brought in rapper Del the funky homo sapien, turned table as Kid Koala, an American hip-hop producer, Dan the Automator."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Songwriting Process for Clint Eastwood
podcast.body: Del the Funky Homosapien stated he helped write "Clint Eastwood" using tips from a book titled "How to Write a Hit Song," which he purchased with a coupon his mother gave him. "Del the funky homo sapien says he helped write the song using tips from a book called, How to Write a Hit Song, which she bought thanks to a coupon his mom gave him."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
